clue.text: Created calm

definitions.meaning: made up or written, as a piece of music or a poem is

explanation.definitionFit: Composing is producing a work, and a composed person is serene and in control.

clue.text: Disturbance in Devon. Roe exaggerated

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs up the letters of the two words, scrambling them

explanation.surface: A commotion in Devon, by someone named Roe, was overblown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbance in' tells you to rearrange DEVONROE. Devon is a county of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdone is taken too far, overstated or overplayed.

clue.text: Stick found by someone in Malaysian bar?

definitions.text: Stick found by someone in Malaysian bar?

parts.words: Stick found by someone in Malaysian bar?
parts.note: a member of the bar in a Malaysian island state would be its barrister, which names a walking cane

explanation.surface: A Malaysian barrister picks up a walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: A Penang lawyer is a walking stick with a knobbed head; 'someone in ... bar' is a barrister, and Penang is a state of Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for a heavy walking cane made from a palm stem in Penang.

clue.text: American writers enter quarters in a state of uncertainty

indicators.note: the American writers go inside the quarters, entering them

parts.note: S and E are two compass quarters, south and east
US is short for United States, so American
pens are writing instruments

explanation.surface: Writers from the USA move into lodgings, unsure of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' puts US and PENS between S and E, two points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is anxious uncertainty while waiting to learn how something turns out.

clue.text: Temptress possibly allied to Hittite leader

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of allied might be arranged another way
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A seductress might have been in league with a Hittite chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' reworks ALLIED as DELILA, then 'leader' adds the first letter of Hittite.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible she betrayed Samson, the archetype of the treacherous seductress.

clue.text: The way to meet an Afg'han

parts.note: a path is a way or track
taken as written

explanation.surface: The road leads to an encounter with an Afghan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to meet' simply joins the two pieces. The scan prints a stray mark in Afghan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pathans, or Pashtuns, are a people of Afghanistan and north-west Pakistan.

clue.text: Conference to secure reduction of figure ?

definitions.meaning: a formal assembly, as of a national legislature
to slim, keeping to a restricted eating regime

explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a legislative assembly, and also a regime of eating designed to lose weight.

clue.text: Contrived to make opening in one end perhaps

indicators.note: the opening is put inside the other letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of end may be shuffled

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: Something devised to create a gap in one tip, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' reworks END as NED; 'in' puts VENT inside I + NED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have invented something is to have devised or made it up.

clue.text: Illegal demand for the tax I once otherwise settled

indicators.note: the letters of 'tax I once' are settled in another order, otherwise arranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests at an unlawful tax demand from long ago, now resolved differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise settled' tells you to rearrange TAXIONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is an extortionate or wrongful demand for payment, a levy extracted unfairly.

clue.text: Tube for the V-one (German type)

parts.note: the letter V taken from 'V-one' as written
the German word for one is ein, which the bracketed 'German type' signals

explanation.surface: A tube designed for the V-1 flying bomb, a German weapon of the war.
explanation.walkthrough: The V-one was the German flying bomb; here V stays as it is and 'one (German type)' asks for the German word EIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein is a blood vessel, a natural tube carrying blood back to the heart.

clue.text: Building used in current strike by male rate collector

parts.note: amp is short for ampere, the unit of electric current
to hit is to strike
he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: the letters of 'rate' are gathered up and collected into a new order

explanation.surface: A building put to use during a strike by a man who collects the rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collector' reworks RATE as ATRE. British rates were a local property tax, and the rate collector the official who took the money.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphitheatre is an oval or round arena building with tiered seating.

clue.text: Literary device employed in Love's Labour's Lost

definitions.text: Literary device employed in Love's Labour's Lost

parts.words: Literary device employed in Love's Labour's Lost
parts.note: the play's title repeats its opening L three times, the very device it names

explanation.surface: A rhetorical technique used in a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Love's Labour's Lost is a Shakespeare comedy whose own title shows the device: three words starting with L.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating the same initial sound in neighbouring words is this figure of speech.

clue.text: Buccaneer finds gold with note in the island

indicators.note: the gold and note are placed inside the island

parts.note: the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea
or is the heraldic word for gold
G is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A pirate discovers treasure and a message on his island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OR and G inside MAN: the island is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Morgan was a famous seventeenth-century Welsh privateer of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Recorder brings girl to heel

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
a ship that heels over is said to list, leaning to one side

explanation.surface: A tape recorder brings a girl to obedience, as a dog is brought to heel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' suggests a musical instrument or tape machine; here it is a person who keeps records.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, chronicling events year by year as a historical recorder.

clue.text: Threats can seem out of place

indicators.note: the letters of 'can seem' are put out of their places, rearranged

explanation.surface: Threats may look inappropriate in some settings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' tells you to rearrange CANSEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Menaces are threats of harm, as in demanding money with menaces.

clue.text: Companion at board meeting

parts.note: board here means meals, so a companion who meets you at meals is a fellow diner in the mess

explanation.surface: A colleague sitting beside one at a company directors' meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' means a table for meals, not directors; a mess is where service members eat together.
explanation.definitionFit: A messmate is someone with whom one regularly eats, especially aboard ship.

clue.text: Noticed old Bob put something in pocket

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
in snooker or billiards, to pot a ball is to send it into a pocket

explanation.surface: An old man called Bob was seen slipping something into his pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is slang for the pre-decimal British shilling, written s. Potting is sinking a ball in a pocket of a snooker table.
explanation.definitionFit: To have spotted something is to have seen or picked it out.

clue.text: Noisy fellow is after the diagram

indicators.note: the fellow comes after the diagram in the answer

parts.note: a plan is a diagram or drawing
gent is short for gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A loud man wants the chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is after' places GENT behind PLAN; 'is after' looks like 'wants'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent means loud and resounding, especially with a mournful ring.

clue.text: Arrange ten clues. for eatable "

indicators.note: arrange instructs the solver to put the letters of ten clues in a new order

explanation.surface: A setter is told to write ten clues for the word eatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' tells you to rearrange TENCLUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Esculent is a formal word for fit to be eaten.

clue.text: No-one out of debt permitted here ?

definitions.meaning: everybody owes money, so all are owing

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it says everybody is in debt; as one, it means given leave.

clue.text: Yachtsman not going to use this canvas ?

definitions.text: Yachtsman not going to use this canvas ?

parts.words: Yachtsman not going to use this canvas ?
parts.note: a sailor who is not leaving stays; the canvas he would hoist is a sail, so the clue joins remaining and canvas

explanation.surface: A sailor who is staying ashore will not need this sail.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as STAY + SAIL: the yachtsman not going stays. A staysail is a sail set on a stay, a rope bracing the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: This fore-and-aft sail is rigged on a stay rather than on a spar, and is made of canvas.

clue.text: Perhaps lost, like the cupbearer

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a tray bears cups

explanation.surface: Maybe the wine servant has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The cupbearer looks like Ganymede or a royal servant; it is the tray on which cups are carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray has wandered off course, so it may be lost.

clue.text: Classically perpetual source of something new

definitions.text: Classically perpetual source of something new

parts.words: Classically perpetual source of something new
parts.note: Pliny's Latin saying 'ex ... semper aliquid novi' says something new always comes out of a certain continent

explanation.surface: A classical author names the ever-flowing source of novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin proverb 'Ex Africa semper aliquid novi' (out of this continent, always something new) comes from Pliny the Elder, hence 'Classically'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman proverb names this continent as the place forever producing novelties.

clue.text: Bit of chicken? That's a funny idea !

definitions.meaning: the forked bone in a bird's breast, pulled apart for a wish
a cheerful, amusing notion: merry plus thought

explanation.definitionFit: Merrythought is the old name for the wishbone, and read as two words it is a jolly notion.

clue.text: It's capital at the end of the road

definitions.text: It's capital at the end of the road

parts.words: It's capital at the end of the road
parts.note: the saying that all roads lead to one Italian city puts it at every road's end

explanation.surface: A capital city lies where the road finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'All roads lead to Rome' makes the capital of Italy the end of every road; 'capital' also suggests 'excellent'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian capital is proverbially where every road ends up.

clue.text: Particular centre of excitement

indicators.note: the letters sit in the central part of the word excitement

explanation.surface: A precise point lies at the heart of the thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes the run in the middle of EXCITEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular is a single detail or entry in a list, one separate article.

clue.text: Mould found at entering building

indicators.note: the word at goes into the building, entering it

parts.note: a temple is a building used for worship

explanation.surface: Fungal mould has been discovered as one goes into a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts AT inside TEMPLE. 'Mould' looks like damp rot, but it is a pattern used for shaping.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or gauge used as a guide to shape copies.

clue.text: Blow up the school in time ?

indicators.note: the school is placed inside the time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone threatens to bomb the school before the term runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ETON inside DATE. Eton College is a famous English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate is to explode or set off an explosion.
